Foma and Eryoma are minor gods in ancient Slavic mythology, specifically from East Slavic mythology. They were considered gods of twins, duality, and opposites. Foma represented goodness, order, and truth, while Eryoma symbolized chaos, darkness, and deception.

According to myth, Foma and Eryoma were twin brothers, born from the primordial god Perun. They played a significant role in the creation of the world, with Foma helping to create the light, day, and goodness, and Eryoma being associated with the creation of night, darkness, and evil.

Their story shares some similarities with the myth of Cain and Abel from Christian tradition, and they are often seen as a representation of the eternal struggle between good and evil. Foma and Eryoma's worship was largely forgotten after the Christianization of Kievan Rus', but their legacy lives on as a fascinating aspect of ancient Slavic mythology.
